act: Marriage, Divorce and Family Relations Act

entries.act: Marriage, Divorce and Family Relations Act (2015)
entries.title: Marriage requires free and full consent
entries.content: A marriage is only valid when both parties freely and fully consent. Forcing a person (including a daughter or son) into marriage is unlawful. A person forced into marriage can seek court protection and nullification of the marriage.

entries.act: Marriage, Divorce and Family Relations Act (2015)
entries.title: Minimum age for marriage
entries.content: The minimum age for marriage in Malawi is 18 years. Marriage of a person under 18 is prohibited. Forcing a child under 18 into marriage is illegal.

entries.act: Marriage, Divorce and Family Relations Act (2015) / Gender Equality Act
entries.title: Right to work and economic independence
entries.content: A spouse cannot lawfully force the other to stop working or to become a housewife against their will. Controlling money or preventing someone from working is a form of economic abuse and can be domestic violence under the Prevention of Domestic Violence Act.

entries.act: Marriage, Divorce and Family Relations Act (2015)
entries.title: Equal rights within marriage
entries.content: Both spouses have equal rights and dignity in marriage. One partner cannot force the other into decisions about work, body, or lifestyle. The law protects against coercion and abuse inside marriage.
